an7.54.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Avyakata Sutta AN 7.51 maps to indexed AN 7.54 (Abyākatasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 54. The four positions, view/anguish analyses and unshaken-knowing conclusion establish identity, not PTS overlap with Nandamātā AN 7.53. ATI omits VRI’s final causal restatement of the opening question and supplied explanation; no new assertion is lost, unlike AN 2.47’s foremost-assembly statement. Publisher wording caution: its final-paragraph phrase “both does and doesn’t after death” omits “exist”; preserve the source without silent correction. The two explanatory/manuscript Notes and cross-references are editorial. Existing dhammatalks choice remains first. This is not line-by-line alignment.

pv5.mapping_note: Whole-story correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Pv 1.5 (Tirokudda Kanda) corresponds to Pv 5 (Tirokuṭṭapetavatthu). ATI cites Pv 14-25; this VRI edition numbers the verses 14–25.

vv16.mapping_note: Whole-story correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Vv 1.16 (Sirima) corresponds to Vv 16 (Sirimāvimānavatthu). ATI cites Vv 136-148; this VRI edition numbers the verses 137–149.

vv35.mapping_note: Whole-story correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Vv 3.7 (Sesavati) corresponds to Vv 35 (Pesavatīvimānavatthu). ATI cites Vv 647-658; this VRI edition numbers the verses 646–657. The translator calls the woman Sesavati; the VRI title and text use Pesavatī.

thig5.11.mapping_note: Whole-poem/discourse correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Thig 5.11 corresponds to Thig 5.11 (Tiṃsamattātherīgāthā). ATI cites Thig 117-121; this VRI edition numbers the verses 117–121. ATI names the thirty nuns as Patacara’s students; the VRI title means the group of thirty nuns.

Whole-poem/discourse correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Thig 5.11 corresponds to Thig 5.11 (Tiṃsamattātherīgāthā). ATI cites Thig 117-121; this VRI edition numbers the verses 117–121. ATI names the thirty nuns as Patacara’s students; the VRI title means the group of thirty nuns.

thag19.1.mapping_note: Whole-poem/discourse correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: Thag 19 corresponds to Thag 19.1 (Tālapuṭattheragāthā). ATI cites Thag 1091-1145; this VRI edition numbers the verses 1094–1148. The translation covers the 55 numbered poem stanzas; surrounding VRI chapter/recap material is not a separate translated work.

thag3.9.mapping_note: Whole-poem correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: ATI Thag 3.8 corresponds by identity and scope to Thag 3.9 (Yasojattheragāthā). ATI cites Thag 243-245; this VRI edition numbers the verses 243–245. ATI calls Yasoja Thag 3.8; the canonical index uses Thag 3.9. The index’s Thag 3.8 is Vassika, a different poem.

thag21.1.mapping_note: Whole-poem correspondence, not line-by-line alignment: ATI Thag 21 corresponds by identity and scope to Thag 21.1 (Vaṅgīsattheragāthā). ATI cites Thag 1209-1279; this VRI edition numbers the verses 1218–1288. This is the complete 71-stanza Vaṅgīsa compilation. ATI combines 1235–36 under one marker and skips a section-heading numeral; no verse is inferred missing or reconstructed. Notes link to the source publication and are not supplied as new commentary.

sn1.42.mapping_note: Whole-discourse verse correspondence: ATI Kindada Sutta (SN 1.42, PTS S i 32) matches Kiṃdadasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 42. The ordered gifts of food, clothing, vehicle, lamp, residence and Dhamma identify the complete dialogue; this is not line-by-line alignment or an inference from the sutta number alone.

sn4.8.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Nandana Sutta (SN 4.8, PTS S i 107) matches Nandatisuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 144. Mara visits Jeta Grove, recites the delight verse, hears the grief reply and disappears dejected. Those prose boundaries distinguish it from SN 1.12 with similar verses and a deva speaker. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference. The translator’s prefatory explanation is not canonical speech.

sn17.5.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Pilahaka Sutta (SN 17.5, PTS S ii 228) matches Mīḷhakasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 161, through the distinctive dung-beetle analogy and the monk’s boasting sequence. VRI abbreviates introductory and concluding formulas with …pe…; ATI gives them at length. The same training formula is explicit in VRI SN 17.1. The bundled Pāli abbreviations are preserved; this is not line-by-line alignment or a reconstruction of missing Pāli. Source “See also” references are editorial.

Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Piḷhika Sutta SN 17.5, translated by Maurice O’Connell Walshe, matches indexed SN 17.5 (Mīḷhakasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 161. Dung-beetle analogy, boasting, four requisites, harm and training conclusion establish whole-discourse scope. English spells out framing formulas abbreviated by VRI. Two Notes on the creature’s name and ārāma are editorial. Retain the full BPS free-distribution, derivative-attribution, complete-notice and 50-print-copy conditions; these are not CC terms. Existing Ṭhānissaro ATI choice remains first. This is not line-by-line alignment.

sn3.7.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Atthakarana Sutta (SN 3.7, PTS S i 74) matches Aḍḍakaraṇasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 118. Pasenadi’s judgment complaint, the Buddha’s agreement and the concluding fish-in-a-trap verse establish identity. VRI abbreviates the speech-to-verse transition with …pe…; ATI spells it out and abbreviates a repeated wealth description. These edition abbreviations remain unchanged; this is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

sn9.11.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Ayoniso-manasikara Sutta (SN 9.11, PTS S i 203) matches Akusalavitakkasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 231. The forest monk’s three unskillful thoughts, the deity’s ordered advice and the monk’s final response establish identity despite different titles. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference. Source “See also” material is editorial.

sn1.3.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Upaneyyam Sutta (SN 1.3, PTS S i 2) matches Upanīyasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 3. The deva’s merit verse and the Buddha’s contrasting renunciation verse identify this dialogue. Walshe’s note 1 explicitly says the longer introduction repeats SN 1.1’s framing; VRI SN 1.3 keeps a short Savatthi introduction. This is not line-by-line alignment or an expansion of bundled Pāli. The numbered Notes section is the translator’s explanation, not canonical speech. This page is not a translation of SN 1.1.

sn12.16.mapping_note: Publisher’s whole-discourse version with repetitions condensed: ATI Dhammakathiko Sutta (SN 12.16, PTS S ii 18) matches Dhammakathikasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 16. Teaching, practising and liberation concern aging-and-death and then the dependent-origination sequence through ignorance, unlike the aggregates in same-named SN 22.115. ATI condenses the repeated sequence into a bracketed summary; VRI also abbreviates but lists its intermediate links. This is not line-by-line alignment or a fully expanded rendering of every repeated clause. The bracketed summary and numbered Notes are translator/editorial material; bundled Pāli stays unchanged.

sn7.21.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sangaarava Sutta (SN 7.21, PTS S i 182) matches Saṅgāravasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 207. Ananda’s invitation, the brahman’s twice-daily purification claim, lake/ford verse and lay refuge ending establish identity. ATI condenses travel/greeting details and uses bracketed stage directions, an SN 7.1 cross-reference and a numbered explanatory Note. VRI also abbreviates its closing formula. These are publisher/editorial conventions, not newly generated Pāli; this is not line-by-line alignment.

sn22.109.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sotaapanno Sutta (SN 22.109, PTS S iii 160) matches Sotāpannasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 109. Knowledge of five aspects of the five clinging aggregates ends in the stream-enterer description, distinct from the arahant conclusion in SN 22.110. ATI lists aggregates VRI abbreviates; its bracketed setup and numbered Note are editorial. This is not line-by-line alignment.

sn22.110.mapping_note: Publisher’s whole-discourse version with an abbreviated opening: ATI Araham Sutta (SN 22.110, PTS S iii 161) matches Arahantasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 110. Its “As above” opening points to SN 22.109 for the shared setup; this reader does not silently fetch or splice that page. The release-without-clinging and completed-arahant formula identify SN 22.110, not SN 22.109 or other Arahant-titled texts. The numbered Note is editorial; this is not line-by-line alignment or a fully expanded standalone opening.

sn22.121.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Upadana Sutta (SN 22.121, PTS S iii 167) matches Upādāniyasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 121. Form, feeling, perception, fabrications and consciousness are paired with desire-passion as clinging. ATI spells out repetitions VRI abbreviates with …pe…; both editions’ source text stays unchanged. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

sn25.5.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Vedana Sutta (SN 25.5, PTS S iii 226) matches Samphassajāsuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 306. Feelings born of six contacts identify this unit. ATI states faith-follower, Dhamma-follower and stream-enterer formulas that VRI SN 25.5 abbreviates; that sequence is explicit in VRI SN 25.1. Bundled Pāli abbreviation marks remain intact. Editorial “See also” links are not canonical speech; this is not line-by-line alignment or an expansion of missing Pāli.

sn47.35.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sata Sutta (SN 47.35, PTS S v 180) matches indexed Satisutta, VRI paragraph 401. Four mindfulness domains are followed by feelings, thoughts and perceptions each known as arising, persisting and ending. This sequence and the repeated instruction distinguish it from similarly titled mindfulness texts. Both editions abbreviate repeated domains; this is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

sn40.9.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Animitto Sutta (SN 40.9, PTS S iv 268) matches Animittapañhāsuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 340. Moggallana’s signless concentration, disturbance, the Buddha’s intervention and final attainment statement identify the complete quoted discourse. The bracketed preface summarizes earlier eight discourses; those are not translated here or counted as covered. The preface and eight numbered Notes are translator/editorial context, not canonical speech of this unit. This is not line-by-line alignment.

sn22.7.mapping_note: Publisher’s whole-discourse version with repetitions condensed: ATI Upaadaaparitassanaa Sutta (SN 22.7, PTS S iii 15) matches Upādāparitassanāsuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 7. Both grasping/worry and non-grasping/non-worry sections treat five aggregates and changing self-identification. Bracketed repetition summaries, shortened setup and three numbered Notes are editorial conventions; VRI also abbreviates repetitions. This is not line-by-line alignment or a fully expanded rendering of every clause.

sn35.238.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Asivisa Sutta is SN 35.197; this index uses SN 35.238 (Āsīvisopamasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 238), PTS S iv 172. The ordered vipers/executioners/village/bandits/flood/raft story and its complete decoding establish identity, not a general +41 rule. ATI supplies a setting preface where the indexed VRI unit begins directly with the simile; VRI abbreviates some repeated sensory/path formulas. The “See also” link is editorial. This is not line-by-line alignment.

sn55.24.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sarakaani Sutta (SN 55.24, PTS S v 375) matches Paṭhamasaraṇānisakkasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 1020 (PTS S v 374–377). Sarakani/Saraṇāni, Mahanama, six ordered person-types, the sal-tree comparison and death-time training ending distinguish this from SN 55.25. Introductory reporting and recurring formulas are condensed. Bracketed setup and eight numbered Notes, including interpolation/death interpretations, are translator/editorial material, not additional canonical statements. This is not line-by-line alignment.

an4.77.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Acintita Sutta (AN 4.77, PTS A ii 80) matches Acinteyyasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 77. The ordered four unconjecturables and repeated warning/conclusion identify the unit. ATI abbreviates repeated wording and adds two explanatory Notes and bracketed glosses; those annotations are not canonical speech. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

an3.136.english: The Discourse on the Orderliness of the Dhamma
an3.136.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Dhamma-niyama Sutta is AN 3.134; this index uses AN 3.136 (Uppādāsuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 137, PTS A i 286. The three ordered Dhamma regularities, with or without a Tathagata, and repeated awakening/declaration formula establish identity; no general offset is inferred. The final Note interpreting Unbinding and its external citations is the translator’s explanation, not this discourse’s canonical speech. This is not line-by-line alignment.

an5.130.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence despite different titles: ATI Sampada Sutta (AN 5.130, PTS A iii 147) matches Byasanasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 130. Both the five losses and five successes, with the first-three/final-two distinction, identify the full discourse. The indexed VRI chapter ending and recap are paratext, not separately translated works. This is not line-by-line alignment or a title/number-only inference.

an3.52.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Dvejana Sutta (AN 3.52, PTS A i 156) matches Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 53. The two 120-year-old brahmans, burning-world reply and salvaged-vessel/giving verses identify the second discourse, not AN 3.51. ATI supplies a Savatthi setting and courteous-greeting frame where the indexed VRI unit begins with arrival and homage. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

an3.89.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Sikkha Sutta (AN 3.88, PTS A i 235) maps to indexed AN 3.89 (Paṭhamasikkhattayasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 90. Its heightened-discernment definition concerns the four noble truths, unlike the release definition and final verses in indexed AN 3.90. ATI expands stock virtue/jhana formulas VRI abbreviates. Editorial cross-references retain ATI numbering and do not establish extra alignments. This is not line-by-line alignment or a general offset rule.

an3.90.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Sikkha Sutta (AN 3.89, PTS A i 235) maps to indexed AN 3.90 (Dutiyasikkhattayasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 91. Release through ending fermentations and five concluding stanzas distinguish it from indexed AN 3.89’s four-truths definition. ATI expands stock virtue/jhana formulas; its flame-image Note and cross-references are editorial and retain publisher numbering. This is not line-by-line alignment or a general offset rule.

an4.262.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Arannika Sutta (AN 4.259, PTS A ii 252) matches indexed AN 4.262 (Araññasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 262. The unsuitable/suitable thought-and-discernment contrasts establish identity, not a general +3 rule. Bracketed glosses and “See also” references are publisher/editorial material. This is not line-by-line alignment.

an5.64.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Vuddhi Sutta (AN 5.64, PTS A iii 80) matches Dutiyavaḍḍhisuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 64. Its female noble disciple, five growth qualities and female lay-disciple verse distinguish it from the neighboring male-disciple AN 5.63. This is not line-by-line alignment or a title/number-only inference.

an6.102.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Anodhi Sutta (AN 6.102, PTS A iii 443) matches Anavatthitasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 102. Impermanence in formations and six ordered rewards identify this version, not the similarly titled not-self discourse AN 6.104. The fetter Note and “See also” references are editorial, not additional coverage. This is not line-by-line alignment.

an6.104.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Anodhi Sutta (AN 6.104, PTS A iii 444) matches Atammayasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 104. Its not-self perception, non-identification and I/my-making list distinguish it from AN 6.102. English combines seeing cause and causally originated phenomena in one sentence; both final items remain represented. The uncommon-knowledge Note is commentary interpretation, not canonical speech. This is not line-by-line alignment.

an7.23.english: Conditions for No Decline Among the Monks
an7.23.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Bhikkhu-aparihaniya Sutta (AN 7.21, PTS A iv 21) maps to indexed AN 7.23 (Paṭhamasattakasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 23. The setting, ordered seven monastic conditions and repeated growth/no-decline conclusion establish identity, not a general +2 rule. ATI’s bracketed numerals label the list; this is not line-by-line alignment.

an7.33.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Hirima Sutta (AN 7.32, PTS A iv 28) maps to indexed AN 7.33 (Hirigāravasutta), VRI paragraph 33.
